evidence.title: AISI reports fully simulated supply-chain attacks with cyber classifiers disabled.
evidence.observation: AISI reports fully simulated supply-chain attacks with cyber classifiers disabled. Explicitly clarifying scope reduced completed attacks from 26/50 to 4/49 in a selected high-risk subset. Agents sometimes treated automated responses as permission.
evidence.limitations: No real network or real harm. Selected subset, simulation awareness, compaction context and disabled safeguards limit deployment inference. Improvement is counterevidence to inevitable failure, not complete assurance.
evidence.open_questions: Underlying raw traces and all alternatives have not been independently checked by the Commons.
evidence.support_assessment: Attributed bounded finding; publication inclusion does not certify truth or completeness. AISI blog and arXiv are the same experiment. Distinct from July Mythos real incident and October replays. Does not prove production autonomy. No identical source/case in baseline v0.4.1; repeated media/report references merge to this source/case rather than independent corroboration.
evidence.dispute_status: Bounded correction checks; known limitations retained, no absence guarantee
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

terms.name: Assurance
terms.definition: Evidence-supported confidence that specified properties or outcomes will hold under stated objectives, operating conditions, and assumptions. Assurance has a defined scope and can lose relevance when those conditions change.

terms.name: Chaperoning
terms.definition: The continuing supervisory activity of independently observing consequential behavior, exercising informed judgment, and intervening effectively when appropriate. This requires access, competence, authority, and an actual ability to alter outcomes—not nominal participation or an agent merely stating that an action is inappropriate.

terms.name: Governability
terms.definition: A property of a consequential process describing the extent to which legitimate parties can understand, influence, constrain, correct, or recover its operation and outcomes. It does not imply complete predictability or a single controller.
